chunks: Ahmad, from Ali ibn Ahmad, from Is'haq ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Daghshi, who said:
I was at the door of Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, so the slave of Shihab came out and said, 'I want to ask Hashim al-Saydani about the hadith of the merchandise and the goods.'

He said, 'So I went to Hashim and asked him about the hadith. He said, 'I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the merchandise and the goods, so he said: Yes, there is none who has merchandise or goods with him except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ordains one who will profit him. So if he accepts (the buyer), or else He directs it to another, and that is because he rejected upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.رَدَّ عَلَى اللَّهِ: Rejected upon Allah (in the context of the transaction)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of buying and selling in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the metaphysical reality of trade, asserting that Allah appoints a specific buyer for every commodity, thereby framing commercial success as a direct manifestation of divine decree (Qadr). This perspective transforms the merchant's role from a mere opportunist to a steward who must discern whether to accept the appointed buyer as an act of gratitude or reject them to avoid 'answering back' against Allah's will. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating spiritual awareness into daily economic activities, viewing profit not as random chance but as a tested trust.

en.hubeali: Ahmad, from Ali Bin Ahmad, from Is’haq Bin Sa’ad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Saeed Al Daghashy who said,
‘I was at the door of Shihab Bin Abd Rabbih, so a slave of Shiab came out and said, ‘I want to ask Hisham Al-Saydani about a Hadeeth of the items and the merchandise’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went over to Hashim and asked him about the Hadeeth. So he said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said the merchandise and the items, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, there is none who happens to have some merchandise with him or an item (for sale) except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Ordains one who would profit him. So either he accepts (the offer of the buyer) or else it is exchanged to someone else, and that is because he rejected upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ahmad has narrated from Ali from Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Sa‘d al-Ash’ariy from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sa‘id al-Daghshiy who has said the following:
“Once I was at the door of Shihab ibn ‘Abde Rabbihi when the slave of Shihab came out and said, ‘I want to ask Hashim al-Saydananiy about the Hadith on “price and merchandise.’”

He (the narrator) has said, ‘I then visited Hashim and asked him about that Hadith.’ He (Hashim) said, “I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about this Hadith and he (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, whoever has a merchandise or goods with him, Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sends someone to profit him. He may accept such profit, otherwise, it is turned away from him to others; it is a rejection of the favor of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.”””
